q: 201. A small window fixed at a greater height than the regular window (generally 30 to 50 cm below the roof level) is called ..........
explain: Ventilators are positioned near the ceiling to allow the escape of hot, foul air and the entry of fresh air, following the principle of convection.

q: 202. A vertical window provided on the sloping roof is known as ..........
explain: A dormer window is a vertical window that projects from a sloping roof, providing light and ventilation to the attic space.

q: 203. The fixture fixed on the external doors where pad locks are to be used is known as ..........
explain: An aldrop is a common door fixture consisting of a long bolt and a slotted plate designed specifically to receive a padlock for security.

q: 204. Joining two wooden boards at an oblique angle is termed ..........
explain: Mitring involves cutting the ends of two members at an angle (usually 45°) so they form a neat corner joint, commonly used in frames.

q: 205. The usual way of specifying the screws used in wood work is by ..........
explain: Wood screws are primarily categorized and sold by their length and gauge (diameter), with length being the most common specification.

q: 206. U-shaped pieces made of wrought iron with pointed ends which are used to connect the members are known as ..........
explain: In carpentry, 'dogs' are U-shaped iron fastners used to hold large timber members together during construction or in heavy trusses.

q: 207. A carpentry tools used for making holes is ..........
explain: A gimlet is a hand tool with a screw-tip and a cross-handle used specifically for boring small holes in wood.

q: 208. A window provided on a pitched roof parallel and slightly above the sloping roof surface is known as ..........
explain: Unlike a dormer, a sky light is installed parallel to the roof slope to bring natural light directly into the room below.

q: 209. A window with a fixed glass provided on the flat roof is known as ..........
explain: A lantern window is a glass-walled structure built over an opening in a flat roof to provide extra light and ventilation.

q: 210. A small wooden block hinged on the post outside the door is known as ..........
explain: A cleat is a small block of wood or metal used to secure a door or provide a stop/grip for a closing mechanism.

q: 211. The window projecting beyond the main external wall is ..........
explain: Bay windows project outward from the main wall, increasing the floor area of the room and providing a wide view.

q: 212. The maximum allowable deflection of a timber beam supporting a roof of span L is ..........
explain: According to standard structural codes, the deflection of a beam should not exceed 1/360 of the span to prevent cracking of finishes.

q: 213. The timber sections of width more than 5 cm and thickness less than 5 cm are known as ..........
explain: Scantlings refer to timber cut to standard sizes with specific dimensions; usually, they are smaller pieces of wood.

q: 214. The projections of the heads or sills of door or window are called ..........
explain: Horns are the horizontal projections of the head and sill of a frame which are embedded into the masonry to secure the frame.

q: 215. A wall constructed to withstand the pressure of an earth filling is known as ..........
explain: Retaining walls are designed to resist the lateral pressure of soil or earth when there is a change in ground elevation.

q: 216. If single coat plastering is adopted what is its minimum thickness ..........
explain: For internal brick walls, a 12 mm thick single coat of cement plaster is standard to provide a smooth finish.

q: 217. In single coat plastering the thickness of plastering should not exceed ..........
explain: A single coat of plaster should not exceed 15 mm because excessive thickness can lead to sagging or cracking during drying.

q: 218. A vertical strip of mortar formed on the surface to be plastered before first coat, is known as ..........
explain: Screeds are narrow strips of plaster applied to the wall to act as gauges, ensuring the final plaster surface is uniform and level.

q: 219. In a three coat plastering the first coat is known as ..........
explain: The rendering coat is the base coat applied directly to the masonry; it is roughened to provide a key for the next coat.

q: 220. In a three coat plastering the second coat is known as ..........
explain: The floating coat brings the plaster surface to an even level and prepares it for the final finishing coat.

q: 221. In a three coat plastering the third coat is known as ..........
explain: The setting coat (or finishing coat) is the final, very thin layer of plaster that provides the smooth, desired texture.

q: 222. In which of the following pointing do the dust and water not accumulate ..........
explain: Flush pointing involves filling the joint and finishing it level with the masonry face, leaving no ledge for water or dust to rest on.

q: 223. As per latest I.S. code the characteristic strength of M 15 grade concrete at 28 days is ..........
explain: In concrete grading (M 15), the number represents the characteristic compressive strength in Newtons per square millimeter (N/mm2).

q: 224. The characteristic strength of a material is defined as the strength below which ..........
options: not more than 5 % of the results fall
not less than 5 % of the results fall
not more than 50 % of the results fall
not more than 25 % of the results fall
explain: The characteristic strength is a statistical value ensuring that 95% of test results meet or exceed the specified strength.

q: 225. The props of from work of the beams with span exceeding 6 m can be removed after ..........
explain: For safety and strength gain, beams with spans over 6 m require props to remain for 21 days according to IS codes.

q: 226. D.P.C. stands for ..........
explain: Damp Proof Course (DPC) is a layer of impervious material (like bitumen or cement) used to prevent moisture from rising up walls.

q: 227. The dampness in the buildings may be caused due to ..........
options: moisture rise in the walls through capillary action
rain beating against external walls and rain travel from wall tops
defective construction such as poor joints in masonry
explain: Dampness can originate from multiple sources including groundwater rise (capillarity), rain penetration, and faulty construction details.

q: 228. A semi-rigid material ideally suited to make damp proof course is ..........
explain: Mastic asphalt is a semi-rigid, durable, and completely waterproof material often used for heavy-duty DPC layers.

q: 229. To facilitate quick flow of a rain water on R.C.C. flat roof towards spouts, it is usually given slope of ..........
explain: Flat roofs are never perfectly flat; a slight gradient of 1 in 40 to 1 in 60 (approx 2-3°) is provided to prevent water ponding.

q: 230. The surface to which the first coat of plaster is to be applied is called ..........
explain: The 'background' is the raw masonry or concrete surface that receives the initial layer of plaster.

q: 231. A series of hair cracks developed on a finished plastered surface is known as ..........
explain: Crazing is caused by shrinkage of the plaster surface, resulting in a network of fine, shallow hair cracks.

q: 232. Few swelling developed locally here and there on a finished plastered surface are called ..........
explain: Blistering occurs when small areas of plaster swell or detach from the wall, often due to moisture or expansion of unslaked lime.

q: 233. The roughening of the back ground surface to provide necessary key for plastering is called ..........
explain: Hacking involves creating small indentations on smooth concrete surfaces to allow the plaster to bond mechanically.

q: 234. The formation of loose patches of plaster due to poor bond between successive coats is called ..........
explain: Peeling occurs when entire patches of plaster lose adhesion and fall away from the background or the previous coat.

q: 235. The complete dislocation of some portion of plastered surface due to imperfect bond resulting in patches is known as ..........
explain: Scaling refers to the detachment of thin layers of the finished plaster surface, often due to improper mixing or curing.

q: 236. A screw with a square head is known as ..........
explain: Coach screws (or lag bolts) have square or hexagonal heads and are designed to be tightened with a wrench for heavy timber joints.

q: 237. Ventilation means ..........
options: replacing the impure air in the building by fresh air from outside
explain: The fundamental purpose of ventilation is the continuous supply of fresh outdoor air and the removal of contaminated indoor air.

q: 238. Air conditioning means ..........
options: cooling, purifying and controlling humidity of air
explain: Air conditioning involves complete 'treatment' of air, including temperature control, humidity control, and filtration.

q: 239. The comfortable temperature range in summer may be generally taken as ..........
explain: For human comfort in hot climates, an indoor temperature between 20°C and 25°C is generally considered ideal.

q: 240. A window designated as 10 WS 15 means ..........
options: a fixed window of size 1 m x 1.5 m
a fixed window of size 0.5 m x 0.75 m
a single shuttered window of size 1 m x 1.5 m
a double shuttered window of size 1 m x 1.5 m
explain: 10 represents width in decimeters (1m), WS stands for Window with Double Shutters, and 15 is the height (1.5m).

q: 241. Stone chips or broken bricks are also known as ..........
explain: Spalls are small fragments of stone or brick that break off during cutting or due to weathering/impact.

options: a putty used in paint work
bitumen based material used for water proofing damp proofing etc.
explain: Mastic is a high-viscosity, bitumen-based sealant used for waterproofing joints and DPC.

q: 243. A facing and shelf, usually ornamental above the fire place is called ..........
explain: A mantelpiece is the decorative frame around a fireplace that often includes a shelf above it.

q: 244. Which of the following is not the standard wattage of electrical lamps?
explain: Standard incandescent bulb wattages traditionally follow increments like 40W, 60W, 75W, and 100W; 50W is not a standard incandescent rating.

q: 245. Which of the following is not the usual size of the ceiling fans?
explain: Standard sweep sizes for ceiling fans are typically 900mm (36"), 1200mm (48"), and 1400mm (56"); 1000mm is uncommon.

q: 246. Which of the following has the lowest bearing capacity?
explain: Soft clay has very low shear strength and high compressibility, giving it one of the lowest safe bearing capacities.

q: 247. Which of the following has the highest bearing capacity?
explain: Hard igneous rocks like granite or basalt have extremely high bearing capacities, often exceeding 3000 kN/m2.

q: 248. Depth of lean concrete bed at the bottom of the footing is ..........
options: equal to its projection beyond wall base
equal to half the width of wall in the super structure
explain: The thickness of the lean concrete (PCC) bed is typically made equal to the horizontal offset (projection) to ensure uniform load distribution.

q: 249. Black cotton soil is often termed as treacherous soil. The reason being ..........
explain: Black cotton soil contains montmorillonite clay which expands and contracts violently with moisture changes, causing foundation failure.

q: 250. For the construction of 10 cm thick brick wall, the bond preferred is ..........
explain: A 10 cm (half-brick) wall is built by laying bricks end-to-end, known as a stretcher bond.

q: 251. The black cotton soil is unsuitable for foundations because
options: it is difficult to excavate it
explain: Black cotton soil has a low bearing capacity and is highly susceptible to volumetric changes (swelling and shrinking) due to moisture variations.

q: 252. Raft foundations are preferred when the area required for all the individual footings is more than ........
explain: When individual footings cover more than 50% of the total building area, a raft (or mat) foundation becomes more economical and effective.

q: 253. The type of steel pile which is generally sunk in soft clay and loose sand of low bearing capacity is ........
explain: Screw piles consist of a hollow shaft with a screw-like blade at the bottom, making them ideal for soft clays and loose sands.

q: 254. The instrument generally used to measure the depth of foundation is ..........
explain: Boning rods are used in sets (usually three) to check levels and maintain a uniform depth or gradient in foundation trenches.

q: 255. The piles driven to increase the capacity of supporting loads on vertical piles are known as ........
explain: Raking piles are driven at an angle (inclined) to the vertical to resist horizontal thrust or increase lateral stability.

q: 256. Which of the following is true?
options: D.P.C. may be horizontal or vertical
explain: A Damp Proof Course (DPC) must be a continuous, impervious layer and can be applied both horizontally (to stop rising damp) and vertically.

q: 257. In ordinary residential buildings the D.P.C. may be provided ..........
options: between ground level and water table level
explain: DPC is typically provided at the plinth level (usually 15cm to 45cm above ground) to prevent moisture from the soil reaching the walls.

q: 258. If the mortar contains both cement and limes as the binding materials, then it is called ..........
explain: Gauged mortar is a combination of cement and lime, where lime provides workability and cement provides strength and faster setting.

q: 259. The advantage of air entrained concrete in lining walls and roofs is ............
explain: Air-entrained concrete contains tiny air bubbles which reduce thermal conductivity, making it a better heat insulator.

q: 260. A cut made in the frame of a door to receive the shutter is known as ..........
explain: A rebate is a stepped rectangular recess cut into the edge of a frame to allow the door shutter to sit flush within it.

q: 261. A flooring made of 4 to 6 mm marble chips is known as ..........
explain: Mosaic flooring consists of small pieces (chips) of marble or colored stones arranged in patterns and set in mortar.

q: 262. The dadoring in bath room should be upto ..........
explain: In bathrooms, dado (wall tiling) is usually provided up to 2 meters (200 cm) to protect walls from water splashes.

q: 263. The ceiling height of a buildings is the height ..........
options: of the ceiling above ground level
of the roof above ground level
explain: Ceiling height is defined as the vertical distance measured from the finished floor level to the underside of the ceiling.

q: 264. Expansion joints in masonry walls are provided if length exceeds ..........
explain: According to standard practice, expansion joints in long masonry walls are provided when the length exceeds 40 meters.

q: 265. In the case of R.C.C. roof slabs covered by insulating layers, the maximum spacing of expansion joints is ..........
explain: For R.C.C. slabs with insulation, the standard spacing for expansion joints is typically between 20 to 30 meters.

q: 266. The lower part of a structure which transmits the load to the soil is known as ..........
explain: The foundation is the lowest part of a building that receives the total load and distributes it safely over a large area of soil.

q: 267. The foundation in a building is provide to ..........
options: distribute the load over a large area
increase the overall stability of the structure
transmit the load to the bearing surface at uniform rate
explain: Foundations serve multiple purposes: load distribution, providing a level surface, and ensuring the stability of the entire building.

q: 268. The minimum load which causes the failure of a foundation is called ............ of the soil.
explain: Ultimate bearing strength is the maximum gross pressure at the base of the foundation at which the soil fails in shear.

q: 269. The safe bearing capacity of a soil is given by ..........
options: ultimate bearing strength / factor of safety
nominal strength x factor of safety
ultimate bearing strength x factor of safety
explain: Safe bearing capacity is calculated by dividing the ultimate bearing capacity by a Factor of Safety (usually 2 to 3).

q: 270. For the buildings on clayey soils, the minimum depth of foundation is ..........
explain: In clayey soils, foundations must be deeper to avoid the zone of seasonal moisture variation; typically 0.9m to 1.6m is required.

q: 271. The thickness of shutter of the door generally does not exceed ..........
explain: Standard door shutters for residential buildings are usually around 30mm thick.

q: 272. The total horizontal force P per meter length of a retaining wall of height H holding a soil of density Y and angle of internal friction φ is given by ........
options: P = yH * (1 - sin φ)/(1 + sin φ)
P = yH * (1 + sin φ)/(1 - sin φ)
explain: Based on Rankine's Theory, the total pressure is (1/2) * γ * H² * Ka, where Ka = (1 - sin φ)/(1 + sin φ).

q: 273. The most extensively used type of pointing in brick and stone masonries is ..........
explain: Flush pointing is the most common because it is durable and does not provide a ledge for water or dust to accumulate.

q: 274. The type of pointing in which the mortar is first pressed into the raked joint and then finished off flush with the edges of the brick or stone is called ..........
explain: This describes the standard application of flush pointing, where the mortar is trimmed to match the face of the masonry.

q: 275. The type of pointing in which the mortar is first pressed into the raked joint and the face of the pointing is kept vertical and inside the plane of the wall by means of a suitable tool is called ..........
explain: In recessed pointing, the mortar is pushed back from the masonry face to create a shadow line and a decorative effect.

q: 276. The process of filling up all nail holes, cracks etc., with putty is known as ..........
explain: Stopping is the operation of filling holes, cracks, and joints with putty or wood filler after the priming coat has been applied to a wooden surface.

q: 277. The width of jamb is ..........
explain: In standard timber door frames, the width of the jamb (the vertical side member) typically ranges between 76 mm and 114 mm.

q: 278. The depth of jamb is ..........
explain: The depth or thickness of the jamb for a standard door frame generally matches the width, falling in the range of 76 mm to 114 mm.

q: 279. In the road works the slump of concrete commonly adopted is ..........
explain: Road construction requires very dry or stiff concrete (low workability) to handle heavy compaction, hence a low slump of 20-28 mm is used.

q: 280. In wooden stairs the thickness of the member used as tread is generally ..........
explain: To provide sufficient structural strength for foot traffic, the horizontal part of the step (tread) in timber stairs is usually 38 mm thick.

q: 281. The bricks used for face work shall be ..........
explain: First-class bricks are used for face work because they have uniform color, sharp edges, and a smooth texture, providing a better aesthetic finish.

q: 282. The weight of the furniture stored in a building is termed as ..........
explain: Live loads (or imposed loads) include the weight of movable objects like furniture, occupants, and stored goods that are not a permanent part of the structure.

q: 283. While calculating the loads, the specific weight of brick masonry is generally taken as ..........
explain: The unit weight of standard common brick masonry is approximately 1920 kg/m³ (roughly 19 kN/m³).

q: 284. The size of the plate used in plate loading test in clayey soils is ..........
explain: For cohesive (clayey) soils, a larger plate size of 60 cm x 60 cm is preferred to capture the settlement behavior accurately.

q: 285. The size of the plate used in plate loading test in gravelly or sandy soils is ..........
explain: For non-cohesive (sandy or gravelly) soils, a standard smaller plate of 30 cm x 30 cm is often utilized.

q: 286. Columns in a workshop supporting Gantry Cranes will have ..........
explain: Grillage foundations are ideal for heavy isolated column loads in industrial buildings where a large bearing area is required to prevent settlement.

q: 287. The least thickness of a stone masonry wall is ..........
explain: Due to the irregular size of stones, the minimum practical thickness for a stone masonry wall is generally 350 mm.

q: 288. The angle of repose for dry sand may be taken as ..........
explain: The angle of repose (internal friction) for dry, loose sand is typically around 30 degrees.

q: 289. The wall constructed across the slope to protect the slope from the adverse effects is called ..........
explain: A breast wall is built to prevent the 'breasting' or sliding of natural earth slopes, whereas a retaining wall is designed to hold back artificial fills.

q: 290. While the depth of the rebate equals the thickness of the door shutter, the width of the rebate is usually ..........
explain: The rebate depth matches the door thickness (e.g., 30-40mm), but the width (the overlap) is usually about 12 mm.

q: 291. In a paneled door, the rails fixed in between the lock rail and top rail are known as ..........
explain: The frieze rail is the intermediate horizontal member located between the top rail and the lock rail.

q: 292. The glass one side of which is patterned while rolling and which obscures the direct vision but does not obstruct light is known as ..........
explain: Figured glass (patterned glass) allows light to pass through while distorting the view for privacy.

q: 293. The most suitable type of door for air-conditioned rooms ..........
explain: Revolving doors minimize the exchange of air between the interior and exterior, making them highly efficient for climate control.

q: 294. The number of steps in a flight should not be less than ..........
explain: A flight of stairs should have at least 3 steps to be easily recognized as a change in level, preventing tripping hazards.

q: 295. The number of steps in an ordinary flight shall not be more than ..........
explain: A flight is generally limited to 12 steps to prevent excessive fatigue for the user before reaching a landing.

q: 296. The extreme vertical support to the hand railing provided at the top and bottom of a flight is known as ..........
explain: The newel post is the heavy vertical post at the start and end of a staircase that anchors the handrail.

q: 297. The under surface of a stair is known as ..........
explain: The soffit refers to the visible underside of any structural element, including the underside of a staircase.

q: 298. The additional support given to the nosing in wooden stair is known as ..........
explain: A scotia is a decorative moulding placed under the nosing of a tread to provide additional support and a finished look.

q: 299. In a stair, the ratio of the vertical distance covered to the horizontal distance occupied by the flight is called ..........
explain: The pitch (or slope) of a stair is the angle between the line of nosings and the horizontal plane.

q: 300. The vertical intermediate support to the hand railing is known as ..........
explain: Balusters are the smaller vertical members that support the handrail and are spaced along the treads.
